basis: Reviewed source statements and published poll blocs, not predicted coalition compatibility.

parties.description: Leader of Likud and incumbent prime minister.
parties.coalition_note: The central party in the Netanyahu bloc reported by N12. Not a completed coalition agreement.

parties.description: Leads the Religious Zionism–Zehut election list.
parties.coalition_note: A surplus-vote agreement with Likud was announced; this is separate from a government coalition agreement.
Counted in the Netanyahu bloc in the N12 poll; this alone does not confirm participation after the election.
Counted in the Netanyahu bloc in the N12 poll, but a surplus agreement with Likud was not signed in the reviewed report.

parties.description: Yaakov Asher is named in the reported joint leadership statement for United Torah Judaism.
parties.coalition_note: No prime minister nomination was promised in the reviewed Pindros interview. Resolving the Torah-student issue is a condition. Not a final joint party decision.
A signatory to the reported common principles for forming a replacement government. Rejected Netanyahu serving as a minister.

parties.description: Former prime minister and leader of Together, allied with Yair Lapid in this election.
parties.coalition_note: After an initial conditional remark, Bennett clarified that he would not sit with Netanyahu. Preserve that correction.
Joined the reported replacement-government principles; publicly rejected sitting with Netanyahu.
Joined the reported replacement-government principles; rejected a government with Netanyahu and his partners.
Offered negotiated support from outside a replacement government, subject to conditions. This is not joining the cabinet or proof that the other parties accept the offer.
A separate Arab party. The reviewed Joint List external-support statement must not be treated as a commitment by Ra’am.

parties.description: Leaders of the Reservists–New Economic Party list.
parties.coalition_note: N12 counts this list in a third bloc. No reviewed coalition participation commitment.

parties.description: Reserve brigadier general and founder of the right-wing Amcha Yisrael party.
parties.coalition_note: A Likud figure quoted by Ynet expressed distrust about which side Winter would join. The reviewed evidence does not settle his coalition alignment.

parties.description: Leader of Blue and White and a former defense minister.
parties.coalition_note: Gantz says he belongs to neither bloc and advocates unity. This does not establish a coalition deal with either side.

parties.description: Leader of the Haredi Public list. His party biography describes him as a Beit Shemesh municipal politician.
parties.coalition_note: Coalition participation not established in the reviewed evidence.

parties.description: Leader of Noam who has served as a deputy minister in the Prime Minister’s Office. This is a past role, not confirmation of a current office.
parties.coalition_note: Coalition participation not established in the reviewed evidence.

parties.description: Leader named for Israel First in the reported list.
parties.coalition_note: Coalition participation not established in the reviewed evidence.

relationships.summary: Likud and Religious Zionism announced a surplus-vote agreement. This does not itself establish a coalition agreement.
relationships.condition: Official CEC filing was not retrieved.

relationships.summary: N12 groups Likud, Shas and Otzma Yehudit in the Netanyahu bloc. This is a poll classification, not an unconditional government commitment.
relationships.condition: The source does not establish each party’s final post-election decision.

relationships.summary: Pindros did not commit to a prime minister nominee. United Torah Judaism links government participation to resolving the Torah-student issue.
relationships.condition: This is an MK interview; the two components must make their joint decision.

relationships.summary: Eisenkot, Bennett, Lapid, Lieberman and Golan published common principles and committed to work together toward a replacement government.
relationships.condition: Prime minister selection and the final governing arrangement remain unresolved.

relationships.summary: Eisenkot, Lieberman and Golan rejected sitting with Netanyahu; Bennett clarified the same after his initial conditional remark.
relationships.condition: These statements concern Netanyahu personally. Their position on a Likud government led by someone else is not established.

relationships.summary: The Joint List offers support from outside a government replacing Netanyahu, subject to negotiations and four demands.
relationships.condition: Crime and security, Arab-locality development, youth programs and a negotiated political horizon. Recipient parties’ acceptance is not established. Ra’am has not made this same commitment in the reviewed text.

relationships.summary: Gantz says Blue and White is outside both blocs and supports unity.
relationships.condition: No concrete coalition partner is confirmed by that statement.

relationships.summary: A Likud figure quoted by Ynet says Winter had expressed support for Netanyahu, but also expresses uncertainty about whether that support is exclusive.
relationships.condition: Which coalition Amcha would support is not confirmed by this report.

relationships.summary: Otzma will not sign a surplus agreement with Amcha. Ynet says agreements can be filed until the coming Friday, 11 days before election day.
relationships.condition: The post is quoted by Ynet. The post itself was not opened.

poll12.note: Published bloc counts, not negotiated coalition membership.

change-platform.note: Published common principles, leaders agreed to work together toward a government.

netanyahu-refusals.note: Bennett clarification, Eisenkot, Lieberman and Golan reactions. Target is Netanyahu personally.

utj-condition.note: Pindros, an MK rather than final joint party decision, gives conditions and no PM nomination commitment.

joint-external.note: Joint List offers negotiated external support with four conditions. Recipient acceptance not established.

gantz-independent.note: Gantz says he is outside both blocs.

likud-rz-surplus.note: Surplus-vote agreement announcement; CEC filing not retrieved. Includes quoted mistrust of Winter.

reported-lists.note: Reported list and leader names, official candidate rank remains held.

surplus-map.note: Report quotes Ben Gvir refusing a surplus agreement with Winter. Original post not opened.

winter-profile.note: Original launch report identifies Winter as a reserve brigadier general and his new party as right-wing. Biography only; August poll scenario not admitted.

gantz-profile.note: Original interview identifies Gantz as a former defense minister. Historical role, no current-office inference.

maoz-profile.note: Historical report identifies Noam leader Maoz as having served as a deputy minister. Does not establish his current office.

leitner-profile.note: Party biography identifies Leitner as its leader and a Beit Shemesh municipal politician. Attribution retained; no independent endorsement.
